30@triton.jit 

31def _split_copy_contig_kernel( 

32 src_ptr, 

33 dst_ptr, 

34 n_elements, 

35 src_begin, 

36 src_period, 

37 chunk_numel, 

38 BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr, 

39): 

40 """Copy one chunk out of a contiguous input in a single linear pass. 

41 

42 For a contiguous input the flat source offset of the ``i``-th element of 

43 the chunk starting at ``chunk_start`` along ``dim`` is 

44 

45 src_off = (i // chunk_numel) * period + chunk_start * chunk_numel 

46 + (i % chunk_numel) 

47 

48 where ``chunk_numel = split_size * dim_stride`` and ``period = 

49 dim_size * dim_stride`` (one step along ``dim`` advances ``period`` 

50 elements in the flat layout). The div/mod pair reproduces that mapping 

51 exactly for every ``dim`` position, so one 1D launch copies the whole 

52 chunk without per-chunk host round trips. 

53 """ 

54 pid = tl.program_id(axis=0) 

55 offsets = pid * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE) 

56 mask = offsets < n_elements 

57 offsets = offsets.to(tl.int64) 

58 

59 src_offsets = ( 

60 (offsets // chunk_numel) * src_period + src_begin + offsets % chunk_numel 

61 ) 

62 values = tl.load(src_ptr + src_offsets, mask=mask) 

63 tl.store(dst_ptr + offsets, values, mask=mask)

94 Each output index is decomposed row-major over the chunk shape, whose

100 pid = tl.program_id(axis=0) 

101 offsets = pid * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE) 

102 mask = offsets < n_elements 

103 offsets = offsets.to(tl.int64) 

104 

105 src_strides = [s0, s1, s2, s3, s4, s5, s6, s7] 

106 chunk_dims = [d0, d1, d2, d3, d4, d5, d6, d7]

109 src_offsets = tl.full([], src_base, tl.int64)

119def split_copy(self: torch.Tensor, split_size: int, dim: int = 0): 

120 """Split ``self`` into chunks of ``split_size`` along ``dim`` and copy each. 

121 

122 This mirrors ``aten::split_copy``: the out-of-place counterpart of 

123 ``torch.split``. The last chunk is smaller when ``dim``'s size is not 

124 divisible by ``split_size``; a ``split_size`` larger than the dimension 

125 yields a single whole-dimension chunk. Negative ``dim`` is normalized like 

126 PyTorch. Every output chunk is contiguous, freshly allocated, and never 

127 aliases the input. 0-dim inputs, out-of-range ``dim`` and non-positive 

128 ``split_size`` (unless the dimension itself is empty) are rejected with 

129 the same error messages PyTorch raises. 

130 """ 

131 logger.debug("GEMS SPLIT_COPY") 

132 

133 if self.dim() == 0: 

134 raise RuntimeError("split expects at least a 1-dimensional tensor") 

135 if split_size < 0: 

136 raise RuntimeError( 

137 f"split expects split_size be non-negative, but got split_size={split_size}" 

138 ) 

139 

140 dim_size = self.size(dim) 

141 if split_size == 0 and dim_size != 0: 

142 raise RuntimeError( 

143 "split_size can only be 0 if dimension size is 0, but got dimension " 

144 f"size of {dim_size}" 

145 ) 

146 dim = dim % self.dim() 

147 

148 dim_stride = self.stride(dim) 

149 out_shape = list(self.shape) 

150 out_shape[dim] = min(split_size, dim_size) 

151 

152 src_strides = [int(s) for s in self.stride()] 

153 dim_stride = src_strides[dim] 

154 period = dim_size * dim_stride 

155 # An empty dimension still splits into a single empty chunk (torch keeps 

156 # one output whose ``dim`` extent is 0). 

157 n_chunks = max(1, (dim_size + split_size - 1) // split_size) 

158 

159 result = [] 

160 chunk_start = 0 

161 for _ in range(n_chunks): 

162 chunk_len = min(split_size, dim_size - chunk_start) 

163 out_shape[dim] = chunk_len 

164 out = torch.empty(out_shape, dtype=self.dtype, device=self.device) 

165 n_elements = out.numel() 

166 

167 if n_elements > 0: 

168 if self.is_contiguous(): 

169 # For a contiguous input the (period, chunk_numel) div/mod 

170 # decomposition is exact for every dim position, so a single 

171 # linear copy covers the whole chunk. 

172 with torch_device_fn.device(self.device): 

173 grid = lambda meta: (triton.cdiv(n_elements, meta["BLOCK_SIZE"]),) 

174 _split_copy_contig_kernel[grid]( 

175 self, 

176 out, 

177 n_elements, 

178 chunk_start * dim_stride, 

179 period, 

180 chunk_len * dim_stride, 

181 BLOCK_SIZE=_BLOCK_SIZE, 

182 ) 

183 else: 

184 rank = self.dim() 

185 if rank > _MAX_RANK: 

186 raise RuntimeError( 

187 f"split_copy supports at most {_MAX_RANK} dimensions, " 

188 f"got {rank}" 

189 ) 

190 # The chunk shape mirrors the input shape with the chunked 

191 # dimension clamped to the chunk length; both arrays are 

192 # padded to 8 entries with zero-stride / size-1 slots so the 

193 # kernel always receives its full fixed argument sets. Order 

194 # matters: strides first, dims second, matching the kernel 

195 # signature. 

196 chunk_strides = list(src_strides) 

197 chunk_dims = list(self.shape) 

198 chunk_dims[dim] = chunk_len 

199 chunk_strides = chunk_strides + [0] * (_MAX_RANK - len(chunk_strides)) 

200 chunk_dims = chunk_dims + [1] * (_MAX_RANK - len(chunk_dims)) 

201 

202 # Kernel-side decomposition recovers the source offset within 

203 # one ``dim`` slice. ``src_base`` only carries the chunk's 

204 # first position along ``dim``: Triton receives ``self``'s 

205 # data pointer, which already includes the storage offset, so 

206 # it must not be added here again. 

207 src_base = chunk_start * dim_stride 

208 with torch_device_fn.device(self.device): 

209 grid = lambda meta: (triton.cdiv(n_elements, meta["BLOCK_SIZE"]),) 

210 _split_copy_strided_kernel[grid]( 

211 self, 

212 out, 

213 *chunk_strides, 

214 *chunk_dims, 

215 n_elements, 

216 src_base, 

217 RANK=rank, 

218 BLOCK_SIZE=_BLOCK_SIZE, 

219 ) 

220 result.append(out) 

221 chunk_start += chunk_len 

222 

223 return result
